images.title: The handkerchief must fit the cloth
images.purpose: Shows a square cloth of area 125 square cm with an 11 cm square fitting inside it, while a 15 cm square is far too big.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Three nested squares sharing their bottom left corner, the largest drawn as a dashed outline.
images.exact_structure: Exactly 3 squares sharing the same bottom left corner. The largest is a dashed vermilion (#D55E00) outline only, side 15 units, labelled 15 cm along its top and 225 cm² near its top right corner. The middle square, side about 11.2 units, is filled teal (#0072B2) and labelled cloth 125 cm². The smallest, side 11 units, is a solid reddish purple (#CC79A7) outline inside the cloth, labelled 11 cm along its bottom edge. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The largest whole number side that fits is the whole number just below the square root of the area.
images.description: Shows a square cloth of area 125 square cm with an 11 cm square fitting inside it, while a 15 cm square is far too big.

image_decisions.why: Drawing the cloth, the too big square and the best fit together shows the decision at once.
